## Context / Problem
Upper-bound wall-clock assertions in tests are the proven CI flake class under runner contention (19d7, 5e94, edfe, 85c3). 15 sites scanned: 13 upper-bound in scope, 2 lower-bound out of scope; 11 currently unescaped. Detector prototype (regex + escapes) caught all, 0 FPs, and found one site manual scan missed (test_lock_stale_reclaim.py:127).

## Approach
DET BLOCKING code-review criterion scanning tests/** for upper-bound wall-clock asserts. Escapes: '# timing: hang-guard — <reason>' line marker, or the existing perf-lane CI-exclusion guard '@pytest.mark.skipif(os.environ.get("CI") == "true", ...)' on the test (the idiom the benchmark tests in tests/scripts/reducer/test_reducer_cache.py:245-249 already use — NOTE: the '@pytest.mark.benchmark' marker alone is NOT an escape — it is registered (pyproject.toml, informational) but no CI invocation filters it out (the suite runs -m 'not integration and not external'), so a benchmark-marked test still executes on CI; the skipif(CI) guard is what actually removes runner-contention flake risk). Migrations (proven by experiment): tests/unit/test_config_perf.py:201 -> spy config._ordered_layers, the miss-path filesystem walk load_config only calls on a _RESULT_CACHE miss (reset_config_cache seam; regression sim caught 10/10); tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py:261 -> exactly one pending_enrichment call + zero drain/spawn. Remaining 9 sites get markers with reasons. Optional follow-on: migrate reducer benchmarks to _api.replay_events spy to restore CI coverage (currently benchmark-skipped). Seed implementation from /tmp/exp4_detector.py; proxy rule: spy the MISS-PATH function, never tomllib (warm TOML cache evades parse spies). Self-exclusion: the detector's own unit-test file carries live upper-bound asserts as RED fixtures, so it is structurally excluded via the sibling guards' EXCLUDED_FILES idiom (scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py:57 — the exact failure b047 recorded when its fixtures self-tripped the comment-hygiene guard).

## Scope
- detector as DET code-review criterion (review-bot checkout) or CI lint per gate conventions
- tests/unit/test_config_perf.py:201, tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py:261 migrations
- markers on the 9 hang-guard sites

## Testing
Detector unit tests: unescaped upper-bound assert -> finding; hang-guard marker escape -> silent; skipif(CI) guard escape -> silent (bare '@pytest.mark.benchmark' without the skipif guard -> still a finding); lower-bound assert -> silent. Migrated tests: regression simulation goes RED (cache cleared per call / drain forced), warm path GREEN.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Detector blocks new unescaped upper-bound wall-clock asserts in tests/** with a teaching message naming both escapes (hang-guard marker; skipif-CI perf-lane guard).
- [x] Both migration sites assert counting proxies (miss-path spies), proven RED under regression simulation.
- [x] All remaining in-scope sites carry reasoned markers; detector run on the tree is clean.
- [x] Detector has unit tests covering fire, both escapes (marker; skipif-CI guard — and bare benchmark marker NOT escaping), and lower-bound exclusion.
